meta.subject: General English -- Class XII
meta.instructions: Tamil Nadu State Board · Higher Secondary Second Year Examinations - May 2022

sections.label: Choose the correct synonyms for the underlined words

questions.html: We watched for a few moments; then as trade <u>slackened</u> we went over.
Individual liberty would have become social <u>anarchy</u>.
He was a walking horror, with a <u>disfigured</u> face and long flap of skin hanging from the side of his neck to his body.

sections.label: Choose the correct antonyms for the underlined words

questions.html: In those days, they didn't have <u>sophisticated</u> heart surgery.
Our father rejected it, saying it wouldn't be <u>sturdy</u>.
We have a whole kingdom in which we rule alone, can do what we choose, be wise or ..... conventional or odd.
Replace the underlined idiom with its suitable meaning. The examinations are <u>round the corner</u>.
options: b) not in the near future

questions.html: Replace the underlined word with a polite form of expression. <u>Slow learners</u> are to be taught with more care and attention.
Choose the word that can be placed before the word <u>drive</u> to form a compound word.
Choose the correct British English equivalent for the American English word <u>Vacation</u>.
Fill in the blank with the most suitable prepositional phrase. ________ rain, take an umbrella.
Choose the appropriate linker and complete the sentence. ________ you book in advance, you cannot witness the show.
Choose the correct word from the options given below and complete the sentence. It was a memorable ________.
Replace the underlined word with a suitable phrasal verb. The fire was <u>extinguished</u>.
Choose the word with the correct spelling.
Identify the correct combination of the word <u>haircut</u>.
Form a new word by adding a suitable suffix to the underlined word and complete the sentence. The soil lost its ________ (<u>fertile</u>) due to excessive sprinkling of pesticides.

options: b) Tamilnadu National People Service Commission

Which of the following sentences is of the pattern <u>SVOA</u> ?
options: b) I ate an apple yesterday.
c) The pot called the kettle black.

questions.verse: "LIKE a huge Python, winding round and round\nThe rugged trunk, indented deep with scars".

subs.q: (a) What is winding round and round?
subs.a: The creeper is winding round and round.

subs.q: (b) Identify the figure of speech in the first line.

questions.verse: "One equal temper of heroic hearts,\nMade weak by time and fate, but strong in will.\nTo strive, to seek, to find and not to yield."

subs.q: (a) Who are referred to as heroic hearts?
subs.a: Ulysses and his mariners / sailors are referred to as heroic hearts.

subs.q: (b) Pick out the words in alliteration in the above lines.
subs.a: heroic – hearts / strive – seek / weak – will (any one pair).

questions.verse: "He will be lonely enough\nto have time for the work\nhe knows as his own".

subs.q: (a) Who does the word 'He' refer to?
subs.a: The word 'He' refers to the son / child.

subs.q: (b) How does loneliness help the person?
subs.a: Loneliness gives him time for his own work and helps him become creative.

subs.q: (a) What is the world compared with?
subs.a: The world is compared with a stage.

questions.verse: "O sweet companions, loved with love intense,\nFor your sakes, shall the tree be ever dear."

subs.q: (a) Why shall the tree remain ever dear?
subs.a: The tree shall remain ever dear because it is tied to the poet's cherished childhood memories and reminiscences of her siblings.

subs.q: (b) What are the alliterated words in the first line?

questions.verse: "It may be we shall touch the Happy Isles,\nAnd see the great Achilles, whom we knew".

subs.q: (a) Which place would they travel to?
subs.a: They would travel to the Happy Isles / unknown world / paradise.

subs.q: (b) Whom would they meet with in the course of their voyage?
subs.a: They would meet Achilles / Greek warriors.

parts.title: Part II · Section 2 -- Do as Directed

questions.q: Reena said, "I am learning French". (Change into Indirect speech.)
questions.ans: Reena said that she was learning French.

questions.q: My request was acceded to by the authorities. (Change the Voice.)
questions.ans: The authorities acceded to my request.

questions.q: I met a man at the party. He is the Chairman of a computer firm. (Combine into a single sentence.)
questions.ans: I met the chairman of a computer firm at the party. (or) I met a man at the party who is the chairman of a computer firm.

questions.q: Unless we plant more trees, we cannot save our planet. (Rewrite using 'If' without changing the meaning.)
questions.ans: If we do not plant more trees, we cannot save our planet.

parts.title: Part III -- Reference to Context and Short Answers

questions.q: 'Without rich wanting nothing arrives'. (Explain with reference to context.)
questions.ans: Poem: 'A Father to His Son'. Poet: Carl Sandburg. The father tells his son that worthy achievement does not come by accident. A strong, meaningful desire and the will to act are needed before anything valuable can be attained.

questions.q: 'This is my son, mine own Telemachus, / To whom I leave the sceptre and the isle'. (Explain with reference to context.)
questions.ans: Poem: 'Ulysses'. Poet: Alfred Lord Tennyson. Ulysses points to Telemachus as the son who will inherit his throne and rule Ithaca responsibly, while he himself longs to resume a life of adventure and discovery.

questions.q: 'Mayst thou be numbered when my days are done / With deathless trees - like those in Borrowdale'. (Explain with reference to context.)
questions.ans: Poem: 'Our Casuarina Tree'. Poet: Toru Dutt. The poet wishes that the casuarina tree may live on in fame and remembrance like the immortal trees of Borrowdale even after her own life ends.

questions.q: What were the various jobs undertaken by the little boys?
questions.ans: The little boys hawked newspapers, polished shoes, sold fruits, worked as tourist guides and ran errands to earn money for their sister's treatment.

questions.q: What happened to the visitor when he sat on the stool at the narrator's house?
questions.ans: The visitor fell down / toppled over / rolled over when he sat on the unsafe three-legged stool.

questions.q: Define 'liberty' as perceived by A.G. Gardiner.
questions.ans: According to A.G. Gardiner, liberty is not merely a personal affair; it is also a social contract that must respect the rights and comfort of others.

questions.q: Complete the proverbs. (a) Variety is the ________ of life. (b) Every dog has its ________. (c) Time and ________ wait for none.
questions.ans: (a) spice  (b) day  (c) tide

questions.q: Rearrange the following jumbled sentences correctly. (a) delayed/denied/justice/is/justice (b) spoil/and/rod/spare/the/child/the (c) time/a/nine/stitch/saves/in
questions.ans:
(a) Justice delayed is justice denied.
(b) Spare the rod and spoil the child.
(c) A stitch in time saves nine.

questions.q: Describe the process of making a glass of lemonade.
questions.ans: Take a fresh lemon and squeeze its juice into a clean glass. Add sugar and a small pinch of salt according to taste. Pour in water, stir well until the sugar dissolves, and serve chilled if desired.

questions.q: Study the lending-library table and answer: (a) How many English books have been lent totally? (b) Social novels are read the most in English and Tamil — True or False? (c) On the whole, which type of books is read least?
questions.ans:
(a) 1737 English books have been lent in total.
(b) False — historical novels exceed social novels in English (True also accepted).
(c) Plays are read the least on the whole.

questions.q: Q41. Answer either (a) Justify the title of the story 'Two Gentlemen of Verona'. OR (b) Describe the situation in the narrator's household before and after the chair was bought.
questions.ans: Option (a): The title is justified by the boys' dignity, sacrifice and selfless labour for Lucia. Option (b): The household moved from embarrassment over the unsafe three-legged stool to pride and comfort after acquiring a proper chair.

questions.q: Q42. Answer either (a) What are the poet's reminiscences of the casuarina tree? OR (b) What is the father's advice to his son when he is on the threshold of manhood?
questions.ans: Option (a): The tree awakens the poet's memories of childhood, lost companions and enduring love. Option (b): The father advises strength, gentleness, desire, independence and creative solitude.

questions.q: Q43. Answer either (a) Develop the hints about Ivan Dmitrich Aksionov. OR (b) Develop the hints about Margot and the children in Venus.
questions.ans: Option (a): Aksionov is falsely punished, spiritually transformed, forgives the real criminal and dies before release. Option (b): Margot is locked away during the one hour of sunshine on Venus and released only after the others realise their cruelty.

questions.q: Q44. Answer either (a) Make a summary of the passage on telecommunication. OR (b) Write a paragraph on 'Value of Time'.
questions.ans: Option (a): Telecommunication enables global exchange of information via telegraph, telephone, wireless and satellites. Option (b): Time is precious and irreversible; using it wisely leads to success and growth.

questions.q: Q45. Answer either (a) Write a letter congratulating a friend selected for a hockey tournament semi-final. OR (b) Write a letter to the Editor about rash driving.
questions.ans: Option (a): A personal congratulatory letter with place/date, salutation, body and subscription. Option (b): A formal letter to the Editor with address details, subject, body and subscription.

questions.q: Q46. Answer either (a) Spot the errors and rewrite the sentences correctly. OR (b) Fill in the blanks appropriately.
questions.ans: Option (a): (i) sisters (ii) senior to (iii) Speaker (iv) consider (v) a useful. Option (b): (i) yearn, earn (ii) would (iii) has already begun (iv) who.

questions.q: Q47. Answer either (a) Develop the hints into a story of about 150 words. OR (b) Read the passage on photography and answer the five questions.
questions.ans: Option (a): A story titled 'Tit for Tat' where the traveller outsmarts the innkeeper. Option (b): (i) From Greek — 'to draw by light'. (ii) Large, cumbersome, lengthy to focus. (iii) By removing lens cover, counting seconds. (iv) To load and prepare a sensitive glass plate. (v) Breaking the seal and loading a roll of film in daylight.
